shots.say: This video was made by democut. You write a short storyboard, your coding agent records the app, and democut edits it into a narrated demo.
shots.say_short: This video was made by democut. Your coding agent records the app, and democut turns it into a narrated demo.

shots.say: Here is Taskboard, a tiny sample app. This is a real browser recording, with a cursor viewers can actually follow.

card.title: Shots that explain themselves
card.sub: Cursor  ·  click ripples  ·  zooms  ·  typing  ·  captions

shots.say: Typing happens at a human pace, and the camera eases in on the part that matters.
Every click gets a ripple and a short pause before it, so nobody loses track of what happened.
Page loads are cut out, and slow parts are sped up to fit the narration. Each shot lasts as long as its voiceover.
Every shot carries a badge that says where it came from. This chart uses made-up numbers, so it says so.
Email addresses and other private text are masked before the page is painted, so they never reach the video.

card.title: How it is made
card.sub: Playwright  ·  Kokoro voice, offline  ·  ffmpeg  ·  MIT

shots.say: A short Playwright script records the takes, and marks a scene around each moment worth showing.
Then one command builds every cut. The voice is Kokoro, running offline on your machine, so nothing leaves it.
From one storyboard you get a full cut, a short cut, captions, a GIF for your readme, and a player page with chapters. It is MIT licensed. Install it in Claude Code with one line.
